definition: Complex reaction time refers to performance on a response task used to assess cognitive function when sustained attention and working memory are involved. It reflects how well a person can respond under more mentally demanding conditions than a simple reaction task.

reasons: The comparison with a simple reaction task and the claim that it reflects response under “more mentally demanding conditions” are not supported by the packet.
The definition goes beyond the packet by generalizing from one study context to a broader description of what the task measures.

The packet supports that a “complex reaction time task” was used and that it assessed sustained attention/working memory in a specific trial context, but it does not support the claim that this task reflects responding under “more mentally demanding conditions than a simple reaction task.”

Several parts of the definition are presented as general meaning of the term (e.g., “refers to performance on a response task used to assess cognitive function”), while the packet only provides limited, context-specific evidence (EPO effects on cognitive performance during experimental hypoglycemia).
